It’s been maybe… I don’t know, a couple of months? Time kind of blurs lately. Ever since that car accident last year things haven’t really gone back to normal, but the last few months have been worse. I’ll be at my desk talking to a client about their policy, and suddenly it’s like I’m back there again—just these flashes in my head of the impact, the sound, the glass. They pop in without me wanting them to, sometimes mixed with these other awful “what if” thoughts that don’t always match what actually happened, but they’re just there, looping.

I feel on edge all the time. If someone walks quickly past my cubicle or appears in the doorway unexpectedly, I jump out of my skin. Same thing if my kids come up behind me too fast at home. I keep misplacing files, forgetting where I put my keys, losing my train of thought on the phone—it’s embarrassing because my job is all about details.

What scares me is I don’t really enjoy anything anymore. Even time with my kids feels sort of flat, like I’m going through the motions. I keep thinking that if my ex-husband had picked them up on time that day none of this would’ve happened, and I get stuck in that sense of dread, like the worst part is still happening somehow.
D018-D016_h001.question_a:
It started after the car accident two years ago. I was driving to meet a client when the truck ran the red light. Ever since, it’s like my brain replays it on a loop. I’ll be sitting at my desk running numbers and suddenly I’m right back there—glass flying, the sound of metal, thinking I was going to die. These thoughts just crash in; I don’t try to bring them up. It’s the same scene, over and over.

I don’t really feel much joy anymore. Even when I’m with my kids, it feels like I’m watching myself from the outside. I used to enjoy little things—coffee with coworkers, closing a big policy—but now it all feels flat.

I keep going over how it happened and I can’t stop thinking it’s the truck driver’s fault and my ex-husband’s too, because he was the one who insisted on that route. The terror from that moment hasn’t faded; my body still reacts like it’s happening right now.

I jump at everything—someone walking up behind me at the office, a quick movement in my peripheral vision. I feel on edge constantly. I’ve noticed I’m more forgetful too—misplacing files, forgetting why I walked into a room—because my mind is always half stuck back at that intersection.

The thoughts are repetitive and intrusive, but they’re always about the crash, and I don’t do any special rituals or behaviors to try to neutralize them.
D018-D016_h001.question_b:
Honestly, the thing that’s bothering me the most isn’t what happened with my ex or the divorce anymore—it’s these thoughts that just won’t shut off about germs and something bad happening if I don’t do things “right.” They pop into my head out of nowhere, even when I’m just answering calls or filing claims at work, and they have nothing to do with anything that’s actually happened to me.  

I’ll be midway through a quote and suddenly I’m convinced I’ve contaminated the whole office, and then I feel like I have to wash my hands over and over until it feels “just right.” At home I check the locks and the stove repeatedly, sometimes for an hour, even when I know I already checked. I tell myself it’s ridiculous, but if I try to stop, the anxiety gets so intense I give in.  

This has been going on for at least a couple of years now and it’s getting worse. I don’t get flashbacks or anything tied to a specific event; it’s more like my own brain attacking me with these random, disturbing thoughts that I try to neutralize with these rituals.

    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
